context.in_practice: The routes differ only when `show` prints a whole map. In route 1 the output contains invisible raw carriage returns: on screen it looks like an ordinary block, but if the output is copied or re-read as YAML, those CRs count as line breaks, so the text comes back changed. Route 2 is exact and unambiguous but hard to read: long prompts appear as one escaped line. Route 3 is readable for CRLF prompts but shows text that differs from the file (no CRs), and it still falls back to quoting for a bare mid-line CR. A file with blank lines at the end prints as a `|+` block on all three routes.
context.stakes: When an included prompt file has Windows line endings (CRLF), a stray carriage return or a leading-space first line, `config show` must still print something. The question is whether that output shows the exact text, stays clean readable YAML, or quietly normalizes it. `config get` returns the exact bytes on every route.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 always prints a block, but the hidden CRs are not true to the file once the output is re-read; route 2 is exact but turns odd files into hard-to-read escaped lines; route 3 is readable but its `show` drops the CRs, and it mixes blocks and quoted strings.

plan_why: show of a mapping holding text includes that a plain literal block cannot hold exactly (CRLF endings, a bare CR, leading indentation, no final newline, extra trailing blank lines) shows whether each route always prints a literal block, prints a double-quoted escaped string, or prints a literal block with CRLF turned into LF; get shows whether the raw bytes stay exact
routes: Double-quoted at first; reworked so every text include is a literal block of the exact text
Literal block with CRLF turned into LF; get keeps the bytes
